I am 64 years old, and I have been farming this land in Quzhou since I was a young girl. I only finished primary school, but I know my fields better than any book. My husband passed a few years ago, and now it is mostly me and my nephew helping during busy times. I have about 6 mu of good flat land, and at my age, I cannot take risks or manage crops that need too much back-bending work like cotton, which needs spraying every week and endless pruning. Everyone around me grows wheat and maize in rotation, and that is what I will do too. It is the safest way — I know the rhythm of these crops by heart. For winter wheat, I will sow in early October after rotary tilling the soil, using an improved variety from the seed shop that my neighbors also use, about 30 jin per mu. I will put down compound fertilizer as my basal dressing and top-dress once in spring when the wheat turns green. I will irrigate three times — winter irrigation, jointing stage, and filling stage — using water from our well. I will spray twice for insects, once for weeds, and once for disease because the damp spring can bring fungus. After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize immediately without tilling again; that is how we have done it for years now, and it saves me labor and fuel. The maize needs two irrigations and about three pesticide sprays total. I expect my wheat to give me about 1000 jin per mu and the maize a bit more, maybe 1100 jin per mu. This rotation feeds me and leaves some grain to sell for cash. I am too old to change what works.
